Security and ACL hook behaviors, capability evaluation and MAC label determination.
Hash parameters, cache sizing, reclaim and grace handling for replaced attributes.
Superblock creation, mount handling, namespace matching and syscall operation implementations.
Inode creation, number assignment, refresh mechanics and dentry aliasing.

findings.text: File creation interface establishes a regular file node beneath a parent using caller supplied name, access bits, ownership, size, operation vector, private pointer and namespace tag, returning a node reference or an allocation failure indication.

New file nodes retain operation vector, size, namespace and private data, optionally enable dependency tracking when a key is given, cache availability of display mapping and release capabilities for use outside active references, and publish through a single add step that releases the node on failure.
Inode operation vector for this filesystem exposes handlers for access checking, attribute update, attribute query and extended attribute enumeration.

Attribute changes serialize with the root wide attribute semaphore held for writing, while attribute queries and access checks hold the same semaphore for reading around inode refresh and generic validation.
Attribute update through the virtual filesystem validates with a neutral identity mapping and applies metadata without honoring requested size adjustments.
Extended attribute enumeration for a directory entry resolves its node, fetches stored attributes without allocating, and delegates to a generic listing routine with a possibly absent collection.

Generic listing combines access control names, security names and stored entries into one caller buffer, supports a size probe when no buffer is given, and reports total bytes that would have been written.
Listing omits trusted namespace entries for callers lacking administrative capability and omits machine access label entries because those are supplied through the security hook.
Access control listing contributes nothing on inodes without POSIX access control support and otherwise advertises access and default entries only when the corresponding in-memory objects exist.
Appending one name accounts its length including terminator even when only measuring, copies when a buffer is present, and signals insufficient space without partial copy.
Enumeration of stored extended attributes runs under read side protection for concurrent updates while skipping filtered names.
Inode eviction discards remaining page cache, marks the inode cleared, and drops the associated node reference.
Access checking reports ECHILD when MAY_NOT_BLOCK is set and attribute setting reports EINVAL when private data is absent.

Stored attribute mutation uses a node keyed mutex instead of relying only on inode exclusion, since a single node can appear under multiple mounts, and this exclusion also guards on demand creation of the holder.

Update outcome depends on prior existence and caller flags: XATTR_CREATE over an existing entry reports EEXIST, XATTR_REPLACE over nothing reports ENODATA, otherwise the operation inserts, substitutes or removes while keeping hash and list consistent.

The shared lookup table is created on first need that carries a value, published with release ordering that tolerates losing a creation race by discarding the redundant table, and value-less requests without a table report absence or missing-data depending on flags.
A complete attribute name is recovered from a suffix by stepping back by the length of the handler prefix.
Virtual filesystem adapters for attribute read and write resolve the full name from handler plus suffix and forward to node level helpers.

User namespace writes report EOPNOTSUPP unless the root enables them, enforce count and byte ceilings reporting ENOSPC on excess, and roll back reservations on failure while releasing quota for superseded values.
Attribute holder with fields ia_uid, ia_gid, ia_atime, ia_mtime, ia_ctime, xattrs and xattr_limits carries ownership, timestamps, stored attribute linkage and quota state.

Root structure holds published kn and flags, identifier allocator with lock, super list, deactivation wait queue, semaphores kernfs_rwsem kernfs_iattr_rwsem and kernfs_supers_rwsem, rename lock kernfs_rename_lock and cache xa_cache plus RCU head.
Super information with fields sb, root, ns and node binds a superblock to its root, a single namespace tag and list linkage within the root set.
A bias constant marks the deactivated reference state for nodes.
Handler table offers trusted, security and user namespaces, sharing common get and set paths except for a quota enforcing set path for the user namespace, terminated by null.
Super operation table provides filesystem statistics, inode release and eviction, mount option and path display, and explicitly leaves freeze and thaw unimplemented.

Option and path display forward to root syscall operations when available, otherwise option display does nothing and path display uses generic dentry formatting with escaping of space tab newline and backslash.

Sequential path output queries remaining buffer space, renders the dentry path into spare room, escapes selected characters as backslash octal triplets, and commits the produced length or marks overflow.
Escaping fails when fewer than four bytes remain for an escaped character, leaving the caller to treat the whole emission as overflow.
Statistics use PAGE_SIZE for block size and NAME_MAX for name length, carry filesystem magic, and derive the identifier from device number then from superblock UUID.
File handle encoding requires two words, reports that need when given less, stores the node identifier, returning FILEID_INVALID when short and FILEID_KERNFS on success.

Handle decoding rejects short or unknown types, accepts FILEID_KERNFS and the two INO32 forms by recombining parts, looks up the node by identifier with ESTALE on miss, optionally moves to the parent with stale indication when parentless, and returns an alias dentry.
Parent dentry construction holds the hierarchy semaphore for reading while materializing the parent inode as an alias.
Export table exposes encode, direct decode, parent decode and parent lookup operations.
Ancestor helper walks upward until the direct child of a target parent is found, warns and yields nothing when child equals parent, and yields nothing when the chain ends early.
File related flags KERNFS_FILE, KERNFS_HAS_SEQ_SHOW, KERNFS_HAS_MMAP, KERNFS_HAS_RELEASE and KERNFS_LOCKDEP distinguish file nodes, cached operation availability and dependency tracking.
Internal header defines a once only inclusion guard macro.
Three globals provide caches kernfs_node_cache and kernfs_iattrs_cache plus kernfs_locks, protected against modification after init.
Quota ceilings SIMPLE_XATTR_MAX_NR and SIMPLE_XATTR_MAX_SIZE bound user attribute count and bytes, and KERNFS_ROOT_SUPPORT_USER_XATTR gates user namespace support.
